biomarkers.name: ER, PR
biomarkers.prevalence: ER positive in ~90% or more; PR positive in ~70–80%
biomarkers.clinical_use: Endocrine therapy is standard; tamoxifen is generally preferred in men with HR-positive disease (aromatase inhibitors are typically combined with GnRH suppression if used)

biomarkers.name: HER2
biomarkers.clinical_use: HER2-positive disease is treated analogously to female HER2-positive breast cancer

biomarkers.name: BRCA2 (germline)
biomarkers.prevalence: ~10% overall (BRCA2 far more common than BRCA1 in male breast cancer)
biomarkers.clinical_use: PARP inhibitors in appropriate hereditary breast cancer settings; genetic counselling

biomarkers.name: Androgen receptor (AR)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Commonly expressed; no established routine AR-directed therapy, though explored in trials

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Almost always invasive ductal NST or DCIS; ILC extremely rare because terminal lobular units are usually absent or rudimentary in the male breast

tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Similar to female HR+ breast cancer

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Rudimentary male breast ductal epithelium (limited lobular development)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Predominantly luminal and usually ER+/PR+; luminal A/B intrinsic subtype dominates, while lobular carcinoma and triple-negative/basal-like disease are uncommon
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Restricted phenotypic spectrum because of limited male mammary tissue lineage repertoire
